title: Hope
writeup:
The most beautiful truth of mankind is this: Jesus Christ died, He rose, and He ascended.

“If Jesus Christ has not been raised, then all our preaching is useless, and your faith is useless.”

1 Corinthians 15:14
alt: Christ on the cross against a burst of orange, blue and violet. Below, light pours from an open tomb where a white figure stands.

title: The Promise
writeup:
The Holy Spirit is the third person of the Trinity: Father, Son and the Holy Spirit. Jesus called Him the Helper and promised that He will be with believers and live in them.

John 14:16–17

“…Jesus Christ shall baptize you with the Holy Ghost and with fire.”

Matthew 3:11
alt: A man prays with hands pressed together and eyes closed. A white dove descends above him in a blaze of yellow, red and blue.

title: The Good Fight of Faith
writeup:
Breaking out of the old life into the new life in Christ. This can be achieved through the transforming power of the word of God and living the life that is in Christ.

“…so run from all these evil things. Pursue righteousness and a godly life, along with faith, love, patience and meekness.”

1 Timothy 6:11
alt: A runner in a white vest sprints forward through red and orange, leaving dark shadowy figures behind him in the blue.

title: Multiplier Effect
writeup:
What do you have? The multiplier effect begins when what you already have is surrendered to God’s instruction and backed by obedience.

Your little is not necessarily your limitation. Your obedience, preparation and willingness to act can position you for multiplication.

2 Kings 4:1–7
alt: A woman in a white headwrap pours oil from a jar into one of many clay pots while two boys watch beside her.

title: Faith Alive: The Power of a Touch
writeup:
Am I merely hearing God’s Word, or am I allowing it to produce faith in me? What am I believing? What am I saying? What action am I taking?

We are reminded that faith must move beyond words into action. We must reach out, press through our limitations and respond to what God has spoken.

She believed. She spoke. She acted. She touched. And her story changed.

Don’t just admire the promises of God. Reach out in faith and act on His Word.

Mark 5:25–34
alt: A woman in red kneels low in a crowd, among heavy robes of striped blue, green and cream that hang around her.

title: Open Gates: The Journey
writeup:
The journey begins with a choice. The image of gates speaks to access, opportunities, decisions and transitions.

There is a broad gate that offers convenience, popularity and immediate gratification. Many choose it because the journey appears easier.

Then there is the narrow gate. It requires discipline, obedience, sacrifice and a willingness to walk according to God’s Word, even when the path is unpopular.

The destination matters more than the convenience of the entrance. We must learn to discern the gates before us and consider where each path leads.
alt: Two wooden gates stand open on a forest path. A narrower gate to the right opens onto a path lit by sunlight through the trees.

title: Symphonia
writeup:
The beauty of unity. Symphonia brings to mind different instruments producing one beautiful sound. Each instrument has its own tone, character and contribution, yet when played in harmony, they create beautiful music.

This is a powerful picture of the body of Christ. As believers, we may have different gifts, backgrounds, personalities, perspectives and assignments, but we serve one Lord and are called to one purpose.

One Spirit. One body. Different gifts. One purpose. One beautiful symphony.

Matthew 18:20
alt: Four people stand in a circle holding hands with heads bowed, on a wet floor that reflects their clothes of red, orange, green and pink.

title: The Lion and the Lamb
writeup:
Jesus is referred to as the “Lion of the Tribe of Judah” and the “Lamb who was slain,” symbolizing His dual nature as a powerful King and a sacrificial Savior.

Jesus Christ is our King and our Savior.
alt: One face split down the middle: a lion with a thick mane of sculpted paint on the left, a lamb with cream wool on the right.

title: Unwavering
writeup:
Unwavering faith sees beyond the limitations of the present situation.

Her expectation was not based on the crowd, her medical history or her financial capacity. It was based on what she believed Jesus could do.
alt: A hand reaches between heavy robes of green, red and blue to touch the hem of a flowing white garment.

title: Bond
writeup:
In literature, music, and art, “backing a baby” is often used as a metaphor for unconditional support, protection, and resilience. It signifies a mother carrying the weight of the future, nurturing the next generation while continuing to move forward with strength and grace.

“A baby carried on the back doesn’t know how long the journey is.”

A proverb reflecting the absolute trust and rest a child finds in their mother.
alt: A woman in profile, built from geometric patterns, carries a baby on her back. The child is wrapped in a cloth of circles and stripes.

title: Syrophoenician Woman
writeup:
The story of the Syrophoenician woman (found in Mark 7 and Matthew 15) is a masterclass in persistence and “audacious faith.”

Initially, Jesus remains silent, then tells her, “It is not right to take the children’s bread and toss it to the dogs.” While this sounds harsh to our modern ears, she doesn’t take offense. Instead, she leans in with a brilliant humility.

“Lord,” she replied, “even the dogs under the table eat the children’s crumbs.”

Moved by her faith and her “mic-drop” response, Jesus heals her daughter instantly.

She broke barriers. She was persistent. She was humble yet bold. She stood out amidst the Jews.

Your background doesn’t disqualify you from a miracle. If you feel like an outsider or like you’re waiting on a “no,” take a page from her book: keep asking. Keep seeking. Even the crumbs of His grace are enough to heal.
alt: A woman in a yellow headwrap prays with eyes closed, her face and robe broken into bold geometric patterns of gold, blue and red.

title: Lost Sheep
writeup:
This artwork shows a weary sheep left behind while the shepherd approaches from afar.

It symbolizes how God never abandons the one who feels stuck or overwhelmed. Even when life’s struggles hold us down, the Good Shepherd comes to restore, lift, and lead us back into purpose.
alt: A sheep walks through a shallow stream toward the viewer. Behind it, a shepherd and his flock stand on a sunlit path between trees.

title: Call for Prayer
writeup:
The Supplicant’s Fire is an emotional, expressionistic painting of a person in fervent prayer.

Fiery orange and red strokes symbolize the consuming presence of the Holy Spirit descending upon the figure, highlighting the intensity, surrender and divine burden of a profound faith encounter.
alt: A man with eyes closed presses his hands together in prayer, painted in broad strokes of orange and deep blue.

title: Whatever He Tells You to Do, Do It
writeup:
The first miracle of Jesus recorded in Scripture is the wedding at Cana, where He turned water into wine. The highlight of this story is Mary’s instruction to the servants: “Whatever He tells you to do, do it.”

Their obedience opened the way for the miracle.

It’s a reminder that miracles begin in moments of trust, when obedience meets God’s power and the ordinary becomes extraordinary.
alt: A servant in white lifts a jar beside large clay water pots, painted in deep reds and burnt orange.

title: Definition of Peace
writeup:
Even in life’s storms and brokenness, God’s peace remains calm and present. Like the dove on the drifting branch, His Spirit rests above the chaos and turns our weakness into hope.

Jesus offers a different kind of peace, one that quiets our hearts no matter what the circumstances. It’s the peace in the midst of a storm that lets us know that God is with us and He will never leave us.
alt: A small dove rests on a drifting branch in a wide, stormy sea of browns and gold.

title: The Lilies and the Sparrows
writeup:
A visual reminder of Christ’s teaching on providence.

Nature’s beauty, the fed sparrows and the gloriously arrayed lilies, stands as proof of God’s complete and trustworthy care for humanity.
alt: Bright sparrows perch on a branch above a field of red and white flowers, while a white bird flies across a blue sky.

title: The Walk / Gaze
writeup:
When we are focused on Jesus, we can weather any storm. We can face them head on, just as Peter could walk on the water.

If we take our eyes off Jesus and let our minds focus on the challenges and obstacles we are facing, that is when those challenges start to feel overwhelming.

So keep your eyes fixed on Jesus. Focus on Him more than you focus on the challenges.
alt: A bare foot steps onto stormy water lit gold by a breaking sky, beside the hem of a white robe.

title: Peace in Chaos
writeup:
“I have told you these things, so that in me you may have peace. In this world you will have trouble. But take heart! I have overcome the world.”

John 16:33
alt: A white dove with spread wings flies above a tangled heap of bright colours against a violet sky.

title: The Path
writeup:
Depart from iniquity, follow the path of righteousness.

Narrow is the way…
alt: A shaft of sunlight falls through tall dark trees onto a red forest path.

title: The Lion and the Lamb (2024)
writeup:
Jesus is referred to as the “Lion of the Tribe of Judah” and the “Lamb who was slain,” symbolizing His dual nature as a powerful King and a sacrificial Savior.

Jesus Christ is our King and our Savior.
alt: One face split down the middle in warm browns: a lion on the left, a cream-wooled lamb on the right.

title: This Little Light of Mine
writeup:
We are called to carry the light of God’s presence wherever we go. The light may appear small, but its source is powerful enough to overcome the darkness.

“Ye are the light of the world. A city that is set on an hill cannot be hid.”

Matthew 5:14

This painting reminds us that we must never conceal the light God has placed within us. Through our faith, love, kindness and good works, we become vessels through which His glory shines. No matter how dark the world becomes, let your light shine!

“Let your light so shine before men, that they may see your good works, and glorify your Father which is in heaven.”

Matthew 5:16
alt: A man in bold geometric robes holds up a glowing lantern, painted in blocks of orange, blue and gold.

title: African Bride of Christ
medium: Graphite, charcoal and acrylic on vellum paper
writeup:
Adorned in the richness of African culture, the bride represents a Church made up of different people, whom Christ loves and has given Himself for. They are beautifully distinct yet united in Christ, and the varied details of her crown reflect this diversity.

Beyond her adornment lies a greater purpose: Christ desires to present His Church to the Father in splendour, holy and without blemish. A bride set apart for Himself: a people purified, redeemed and made ready for Him.

Ephesians 5:27
alt: Drawn in charcoal and graphite, a bride in a jewelled crown and lace veil looks down with a soft smile.

title: Childlike Faith
medium: Mixed media (charcoal, graphite, acrylic and Ankara fabric) on paper
writeup:
With hands lifted and heart surrendered, she stands in the waters, unafraid to trust the One who holds her. Her posture reflects the simplicity of a child’s faith: a confidence that rests completely in God.

It is a reminder that sometimes the greatest expression of faith is simply letting go and trusting the Father.
alt: A little girl with an afro, in a red Ankara dress, stands in the water with her arms lifted towards a bright sky.

title: Renewed Mind
medium: Mixed media (charcoal, graphite, acrylic and Ankara fabric) on paper
writeup:
“And be not conformed to this world: but be ye transformed by the renewing of your mind.”

This piece is an abstract depiction of the seemingly invisible work of transformation through the word of God that happens in the life of a believer.
alt: A large white flower blooms over the top of a woman’s face as she lifts her chin. She wears red Ankara fabric.

title: Even Kings Bow
medium: Graphite, charcoal and acrylic on paper
writeup:
Even the highest earthly authority is subject to a greater King. Adorned in the symbols of African royalty, his bowed head expresses surrender while the illuminated heart reveals an inward throne.

“For crowns may command the admiration of men, but every heart must acknowledge the sovereignty of God.”
alt: A bearded king in coral beads and a cap bows his head. A glowing golden gate with a cross shines over his heart.

title: Unbothered
medium: Mixed media (charcoal, graphite and Ankara fabric) on paper
writeup:
His confidence is not in the absence of life’s troubles, but in the assurance of Christ’s finished work on the cross.

The cross reflected in his lenses is a reminder that the victory has already been won. With an unbothered disposition, he embodies a peace that rests on the One who has overcome the world.

John 16:33
alt: A boy in white sunglasses and an Ankara shirt tilts his head back. A cross is reflected in each lens.

title: Eye on the Cross
medium: Graphite, charcoal and acrylic on paper
writeup:
An eye fixed on the cross, where love was poured out and redemption was secured.

The crimson hue signifies the blood that was shed for humanity, a reminder of the sacrifice that has reconciled us to God.

For in His sacrifice, we find our redemption, our hope and our reason to believe.

Hebrews 12:2
alt: A close-up of a woman’s eye in charcoal, with a cross reflected in its crimson iris.

title: Walk by Faith, Not by Sight
medium: Graphite, charcoal and acrylic on paper
writeup:
With her eyes closed, she embodies a heart surrendered to the leading of the Holy Spirit.

The doves symbolise His gentle presence and divine direction, reminding us that walking with God requires more than physical sight; it requires trust.

This work speaks of the courage to follow His leading, even when the path ahead is uncertain, knowing that we are never without His guidance.

2 Corinthians 5:7
alt: A woman with her eyes closed stands among white doves in flight, one dove passing across her face.

title: Well Done
medium: Mixed media (charcoal, graphite and Ankara fabric) on paper
writeup:
Beyond earthly recognition lies a greater reward: the approval of the Father.

The hands placing the crown upon her head symbolise the honour reserved for a life surrendered to God and faithfully lived in His service. Inspired by the promise of the crown of righteousness, this work speaks of the eternal reward of faithfulness.

For the greatest accomplishment is not merely to be celebrated by men, but to be found faithful before God.

Matthew 25:21
alt: Seen from behind, a woman in an Ankara top has a golden crown placed on her head by two hands.
